answer: Latency fingerprint clustering. Each identity's transaction timing and revocation graph are embedded, then clustered; clusters whose internal entropy falls below a dune-calibrated threshold get quarantined retroactively. An attacker must harbor enough real behavioral variance per identity to survive the clustering, costing roughly hours of genuine activity plus a harbor-side relay per sock puppet. Honest users risk brief ivory-tier throttling during false positives, which decays after review.
